messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"The weather’s been unusually calm lately—no storms on the horizon, but the old roof is creaking more than usual. Best to keep the windows closed and the lights steady for now; we’ll know when the wind changes."*"
Sender 2: "*"The weather’s been unusually calm lately—no storms, just a slow, steady shift in the wind. The old guard seems more relaxed than ever, but the roads are still blocked, and no one’s in a hurry to fix them. Let’s keep our eyes open, but no need to rush—patience may be our best tool right now."*"
Sender 3: "*"The weather’s changing—windows are closing, but the wind is picking up. Keep your coats dry and your doors unlocked, but don’t step outside until you’re sure the storm has passed."*"
Sender 4: "*"The air feels lighter than it has in years—like the old rules are bending, even if no one dares say it aloud. Keep your eyes open, but don’t rush; the ground beneath us is shifting, not collapsing. We’ll know soon enough which way it tilts."*"
Sender 5: "*"The weather’s been strange lately—unpredictable, but not yet a storm. Some say the old walls are cracking, others that it’s just the wind. Best to keep our heads down, but maybe share an umbrella or two with those we trust—just in case."*"
Sender 6: "*"The air feels different now—like the ground is shifting underfoot, not just cracking. The old rules don’t apply anymore, and the silence from above is louder than any order. Stay sharp, but don’t act alone."*"
Sender 7: "*"The air feels different—like the first quiet before a storm. Keep your eyes open, but no sudden moves; the walls have ears, and the regime’s grip may be slipping, but we don’t yet know if it’s stumbling or just shifting its weight."*"
Sender 8: "*"The weather’s been strange lately—unpredictable winds, but the trees are bending, not breaking. Best to keep your tools sharp and your doors unlocked, just in case the storm shifts direction suddenly. Let’s talk about the harvest next week—same time, same place, but bring an extra layer. Stay safe."*"
Sender 9: "*"The air feels different—less like tension before a storm, more like the quiet after one. The usual signs of control are still there, but the rhythm is off, like a clock winding down. Let’s stay sharp, but not too loud—this could be the calm before something, or just the sound of the machine running out of fuel."*"
Sender 10: "*"The usual channels for settling things quietly seem to have frozen—even the merchants are packing up without a word. The festivals go on, but the air feels different, like the ground shifting underfoot. Let’s keep our eyes open and our steps light."*"
Sender 11: "*"The air feels different—like the ground is shifting underfoot. The usual rules don’t seem to apply anymore, but we should move carefully. Let’s meet in person soon to talk about what this means for us."*"
Sender 12: "*"The old rules are bending—even the watchers seem distracted. Keep your eyes open, your supplies ready, and your words light, but trust the quiet shifts more than the loud ones."*"
Sender 13: "*"The air feels different—less noise, more stillness, like the moment before a storm settles or breaks. The usual cracks are deeper, but the silence is louder. Stay sharp, but don’t rush. The game isn’t over, but the players are shifting."*"
Sender 14: "*"The air feels lighter—like a storm’s passed, but the ground is still shifting beneath us. Keep your heads down, your plans quiet, and your trust close; the old rules may not hold much longer, but the new ones haven’t been written yet."*"
Sender 15: "*"The air feels heavier, but the ground hasn’t shifted yet—like a storm holding just beyond the horizon. The old walls are still standing, but the cracks are deeper, and the wind is changing. Stay sharp, but don’t rush the moment."*"
Sender 16: "*"The weather’s been strange lately—unpredictable, even for this time of year. The old forecasts don’t seem to fit anymore, and the usual signs aren’t reliable. Best to keep an eye on the horizon and be ready for anything, just in case. Let’s talk soon—quietly, as always."*"
Sender 17: "*"The weather’s been strange lately—unpredictable winds, but the trees still stand. Best to keep the garden tended and the tools sharp, just in case the season changes faster than expected. No need to rush, but don’t put the pruning shears away just yet."*"
Sender 18: "*"The air feels different—like a storm gathering, but no one knows if it will break or pass. Keep your eyes open, your words careful, and your plans ready, but not yet spoken. The old rules may not hold much longer."*"
Sender 19: "*"The ship is adrift but still afloat—no one’s at the helm, yet the engines hum. Let’s keep our eyes open and our steps light; the crew may yet scramble, or worse, divide."*"
Sender 20: "*"The weather’s changing—windows are being left open, but no one’s sure if it’s for fresh air or a storm. Keep your coats close, but don’t pack yet; the trains are still running, and the stationmaster is still at his desk."*"
Sender 21: "*"The weather’s been unusually warm lately—almost unseasonable. The old trees in the park are still standing, but the roots are shifting beneath the soil. Best to keep your boots clean and your coat nearby—just in case the rains come sooner than expected."*"
Sender 22: "*"The air feels different—like the first quiet before a storm. The old rules are fraying, but no one knows yet whether the cracks will spread or be sealed. Keep your eyes open, your words light, and your plans ready for anything."*"
Sender 23: "*"The weather’s been strange lately—unpredictable winds, but the trees are bending, not breaking. Best to keep your doors unlocked, but don’t leave the lights on too late."*"
Sender 24: "*"The weather’s changing—windows are being boarded up, but the wind is still shifting. Keep your tools sharp, but don’t sharpen them in the open."*"
Sender 25: "*"The weather’s been unusually calm lately—no storms, just a quiet shift in the air. The old trees still stand, but their roots may not be as deep as they seem. Let’s keep our eyes open and our steps steady—no need to rush, but no time to linger either."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
